description: What a NEW project should be, per stack. config/stack-mappings.json answers the opposite question — 'what is this repo?' — by matching indicator files. These are two different acts: detection is a measurement, a baseline is a decision, and merging them would make it impossible to tell a recorded choice from an observed fact. Keyed to the same stack ids so a reader can join them.

versionPolicy.rule: Every version below is a recorded value with a date and a source, never a live measurement. State the recorded value AND the version you actually observe in the toolchain, and name which is which. An agent that reports only the recorded number is quoting this file back at itself, which is not evidence.
versionPolicy.onDrift: When the observed toolchain is NEWER than the recorded minimum, use the observed one and say so — the minimum is a floor, not a ceiling. When it is OLDER, that is a finding: report it, do not silently downgrade the design, and do not propose an API the project cannot compile. When the gap is more than one major, say plainly that this file is stale rather than pretending the number is current.

sourceMeaning.measured: Read from a live toolchain or lockfile on verifiedOn. Trustworthy.
sourceMeaning.user-directed: The user stated this explicitly. Binding regardless of what a corpus or a default says.
sourceMeaning.model-recall: Written from the authoring model's training knowledge, NOT checked against a release feed. Treat as a plausible floor and verify before quoting it to anyone. This is the weakest source in the file and most entries carry it.

precedence.greenfield: PRESCRIPTIVE. There is no repository convention to defer to yet, so this file supplies one. Departing from it is a decision that gets recorded as an ADR via scripts/decision.py, not a silent choice.
precedence.brownfield: ADVISORY ONLY. Report the gap between the baseline and what the repo does; never rewrite working code to close it, and never introduce a second mechanism alongside an existing one. A migration is its own decision with its own ADR.
precedence.repoOverride: A consumer repository's own CLAUDE.md or copilot-instructions.md outranks every value in this file, in both directions. A hub that overrides a team's stated convention is a hub that gets uninstalled.

concerns.requirement: Structured logging with a correlation id propagated across every boundary, plus traces and metrics exported through a vendor-neutral API.
concerns.why: Retrofitting correlation ids means touching every call site at once. It costs almost nothing on day one and is a multi-week project after the first incident.

concerns.requirement: Separate liveness and readiness signals. Readiness must actually check the dependencies the service cannot serve without.
concerns.why: A liveness probe that returns 200 because the process is running will keep a service in the load balancer while every request fails on a dead database.

concerns.requirement: Bound once into a typed object and validated at startup. No untyped key lookups deep in business logic.
concerns.why: A typo in an untyped config key becomes a null at three in the morning instead of a failure to start.

concerns.requirement: Secrets come from an external store or injected environment. Never committed, never defaulted to a working value in source.
concerns.why: A secret with a working default in source gets deployed as-is, and the commit that introduced it is the one nobody reviews closely.

concerns.requirement: Deny by default. Authorization decided at a single enforcement point, not scattered across handlers.
concerns.why: Allow-by-default plus per-handler checks means every new endpoint is unprotected until someone remembers. The failure is silent and looks like working code.

concerns.requirement: Validated at the boundary against an explicit schema, before it reaches domain logic.
concerns.why: Validation spread through the domain layer cannot be audited, and the one path that skipped it is the one that gets found.

concerns.requirement: A typed, documented error shape. Never a raw stack trace or an internal exception message to a client.
concerns.why: Stack traces leak framework versions, file paths, and query structure — reconnaissance handed over for free.

concerns.requirement: Every outbound call carries an explicit timeout. Retries use exponential backoff with jitter and are applied only to idempotent operations.
concerns.why: A missing timeout turns one slow dependency into thread-pool exhaustion. Retries without jitter turn a blip into a synchronised stampede.

concerns.requirement: Versioned, source-controlled, forward-only, and reviewed like code. Expand-then-contract for anything that breaks a running deployment.
concerns.why: A schema change applied by hand cannot be rolled back or reproduced in another environment, and nobody can tell which environments received it.

concerns.requirement: Unit tests on domain logic, integration tests against a real dependency rather than a mock of it, and end-to-end coverage of the critical user paths.
concerns.why: A suite that mocks the database proves the mock works. The bugs that reach production live in the seam that mocking removed.

concerns.requirement: A committed lockfile, automated dependency vulnerability scanning, and a generated SBOM.
concerns.why: Without a lockfile the build is not reproducible, so the artifact that passed CI is not provably the artifact that shipped.

concerns.requirement: Build, test, lint, and a security scan all pass before merge, enforced by the platform rather than by convention.
concerns.why: A gate that relies on people remembering is not a gate. It holds until the first urgent Friday deploy.

concerns.requirement: Versioned and machine-readable, generated from the code rather than maintained beside it.
concerns.why: Hand-maintained API docs drift within weeks, and a consumer that trusts them breaks in a way the producer cannot reproduce.

concerns.requirement: A documented, exercised rollback path — including what happens to data written by the version being rolled back.
concerns.why: A rollback plan first attempted during an incident is a hypothesis, and the data written by the bad version is the part it usually forgets.

baselines.name: .NET service (command and query sides)

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.cadence: One major each November; even-numbered majors are LTS with 3 years support, odd are STS with 18 months.

architecture.default: Modular monolith organised in vertical slices — one feature owns its endpoint, handler, validation, and persistence together. Split CQRS onto separate read and write models only where the read genuinely diverges from the write.
architecture.why: A vertical slice keeps everything a change touches in one folder, so the blast radius of a feature is visible in the directory tree. A modular monolith gets the module boundaries of microservices without paying for a network hop and a distributed transaction before there is any evidence that either is needed. CQRS applied uniformly to every entity is ceremony: most entities read the way they write.
architecture.escalateTo: Extract a module into its own service when it needs an independent deploy cadence or independent scaling AND owns data no other module reads directly. Two of the three is not enough — the network boundary costs more than the coupling it removes.

modernCapabilities.insteadOf: MVC controllers for new services
modernCapabilities.note: TypedResults keeps the response type in the signature, so OpenAPI generation stops guessing.

Mutable DTO classes with settable properties

modernCapabilities.note: Optional. Adopt it for multi-service solutions; it is overhead for a single service.

modernCapabilities.insteadOf: Tracking every entity on a read-only query

forbiddenDependencies.reason: Commercially licensed from v12. The in-process dispatch surface a vertical-slice codebase actually needs is roughly forty lines, which is a poor trade for a paid dependency sitting on every request path.
forbiddenDependencies.instead: A hand-rolled dispatcher: an ICommandHandler<TCommand,TResult> interface, DI registration by assembly scan, and a thin ISender that resolves and invokes. Keep the pipeline-behaviour concept if you use it.

forbiddenDependencies.reason: Commercially licensed, and reflection-based mapping moves a field-name mismatch from compile time to runtime — the failure surfaces as a silently null property rather than a build error.
forbiddenDependencies.instead: Explicit mapping methods, or a source generator such as Mapperly which produces readable code you can step through.

forbiddenDependencies.reason: Relicensed commercially for most commercial use at v8.
forbiddenDependencies.instead: Stay on the last permissive version, or move to Shouldly, or use xUnit/TUnit assertions directly.

forbiddenDependencies.reason: Not deprecated, but slower and unable to participate in source-generated or AOT-compatible serialization. Taking it in a new project forecloses Native AOT.
forbiddenDependencies.instead: System.Text.Json. Keep Newtonsoft only where a specific converter has no equivalent, and isolate it.

concernImplementations.observability: OpenTelemetry via the OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting packages, with ILogger structured logging and W3C trace context propagated by the default HttpClient handler.
concernImplementations.health-and-readiness: AddHealthChecks with tagged checks; map /health/live filtered to no dependencies and /health/ready to the tagged dependency set.
concernImplementations.secrets-management: User Secrets locally; a managed secret store injected as configuration in every deployed environment. Never appsettings.json.
concernImplementations.authn-authz: Authentication middleware plus authorization policies; RequireAuthorization() applied at the endpoint-group level so a new endpoint inherits protection by default.
concernImplementations.input-validation: FluentValidation or DataAnnotations executed in a dispatcher pipeline step before the handler runs.
concernImplementations.error-contract: ProblemDetails (RFC 9457) via AddProblemDetails and a global exception handler; the exception message never reaches the response body in a non-development environment.
concernImplementations.resilience: AddStandardResilienceHandler on every typed HttpClient — it supplies timeout, retry with jitter, and a circuit breaker together.
concernImplementations.data-migrations: EF Core migrations committed to source; applied by a deployment step or a dedicated migration job, never by the application at startup in production.
concernImplementations.testing: xUnit or TUnit for unit tests; WebApplicationFactory plus Testcontainers for integration tests against a real database engine.
concernImplementations.supply-chain: Central Package Management via Directory.Packages.props, a committed packages.lock.json, and dotnet list package --vulnerable in CI.
concernImplementations.ci-gate: dotnet build with warnings as errors, dotnet test, dotnet format --verify-no-changes, and a vulnerability scan, all required for merge.
concernImplementations.api-contract: OpenAPI generated from the endpoint signatures via the built-in Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi, versioned with Asp.Versioning.
concernImplementations.rollback: Expand-then-contract migrations so the previous application version still runs against the new schema; document the data-repair step for anything the rolled-back version wrote.

baselines.notes: The MediatR and AutoMapper entries are the two most likely to be argued with, because both were the default advice for a decade and both still appear in most tutorials. State the licence reason explicitly rather than presenting the hand-rolled dispatcher as if it were the conventional choice.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.minimum: netstandard2.0 plus a current net10.0 target

architecture.default: Multi-targeted library with a deliberately small public surface. Everything not explicitly part of the contract is internal.
architecture.why: A library's public surface is its irreversible decision — every exported type is a compatibility obligation. Multi-targeting lets consumers on older runtimes adopt it without forcing a framework upgrade, which is usually why a shared library fails to get adopted.
architecture.escalateTo: Split into separate packages when one consumer needs a fraction of the library and is forced to take a heavy transitive dependency for the rest.

modernCapabilities.insteadOf: Runtime reflection
modernCapabilities.note: Reflection in a library forecloses Native AOT for every consumer, not just for you.

modernCapabilities.use: Public API analyzers with committed .api.txt baselines
modernCapabilities.insteadOf: Reviewing surface changes by eye

modernCapabilities.use: Deterministic builds with SourceLink and a published symbol package
modernCapabilities.insteadOf: Shipping a binary consumers cannot step into

forbiddenDependencies.reason: A library's dependencies become every consumer's dependencies, and a version conflict between two libraries is unresolvable by the consumer.
forbiddenDependencies.instead: Depend on abstractions from Microsoft.Extensions.* where possible; take nothing that pins a major version of a widely used package.

concernImplementations.observability: Accept an ILogger<T> or ILoggerFactory; never construct a logging pipeline inside a library. Expose an ActivitySource and an EventSource/Meter for consumers to subscribe to.
concernImplementations.configuration: An options class the consumer binds. A library that reads IConfiguration directly steals a decision from its host.
concernImplementations.error-contract: Purpose-built exception types deriving from a single library base exception, so a consumer can catch the library without catching everything.
concernImplementations.testing: xUnit or TUnit against every target framework in the multi-target set, not just the newest.
concernImplementations.supply-chain: Deterministic build, SourceLink, published .snupkg, and a generated SBOM attached to the release.
concernImplementations.ci-gate: Build, test across all targets, public-API baseline diff, and pack — all required for merge.
concernImplementations.api-contract: SemVer enforced by the public API analyzer; a major bump is required for any removal or signature change.
concernImplementations.rollback: Never unlist-and-replace a published version. Ship a new patch — consumers may already have restored the bad one.
concernImplementations.secrets-management: Not applicable — a library must never read a secret store directly; it receives credentials from its host.
concernImplementations.health-and-readiness: Not applicable to a library. Expose a diagnostic method the host can surface in its own health check.
concernImplementations.authn-authz: Not applicable — a library must not make authorization decisions on its host's behalf.
concernImplementations.input-validation: Validate public method arguments and throw ArgumentException early; a library cannot trust its caller.
concernImplementations.resilience: Expose timeout and retry as options rather than hardcoding them — the host owns its own failure policy.
concernImplementations.data-migrations: Not applicable unless the library owns schema, in which case it ships migrations the host chooses when to apply.

testing.unit: xUnit or TUnit across every target framework
testing.integration: A consuming sample project built in CI

baselines.name: Angular

runtime.name: Angular
runtime.knownLatestAtAuthoring: 20 as directed by the user; the release cadence means 21 or 22 may have shipped by the time you read this
runtime.cadence: Two majors a year, roughly May and November — this number rots faster than any other in this file. Read @angular/core in package.json and trust that over this entry.

architecture.default: Standalone components throughout, signal-based state, lazy-loaded feature routes, and a thin typed data-access layer per feature. No NgModules in new code.
architecture.why: Standalone components declare their own dependencies, so a component's imports list is its actual dependency graph rather than whatever its NgModule happened to pull in. Signals make change detection dependency-tracked rather than tree-walking, which is what makes zoneless viable and removes the OnPush-versus-default cognitive tax.
architecture.escalateTo: Introduce a store library only when server state and client state genuinely diverge — optimistic updates, cross-route caching, undo. Signals plus a service cover more than most teams expect, and adding a second state mechanism alongside them is a decision, not a detail.
layers: Presentational components (signal inputs, OnPush or zoneless)

modernCapabilities.insteadOf: BehaviorSubject plus async pipe for local component state

modernCapabilities.use: input(), output(), model() and signal queries (viewChild, contentChild)
modernCapabilities.insteadOf: @Input()/@Output() decorators and @ViewChild
modernCapabilities.note: input.required<T>() moves a missing binding to a compile-time error under strictTemplates.

modernCapabilities.insteadOf: *ngIf, *ngFor, *ngSwitch
modernCapabilities.note: @for requires track — it is not optional and it is the whole performance point.

modernCapabilities.insteadOf: Manual dynamic import plus a loading flag

HttpClientModule

forbiddenDependencies.id: A global state library adopted by default
forbiddenDependencies.reason: Adopting a store before there is cross-feature shared state produces boilerplate proportional to the app with no corresponding benefit, and it is very hard to remove later.
forbiddenDependencies.instead: Signals plus a scoped service. Introduce NgRx SignalStore or similar only when the escalation trigger above is genuinely met, and record it as an ADR.

forbiddenDependencies.reason: In maintenance mode by its own maintainers, and large.
forbiddenDependencies.instead: date-fns, Luxon, or the platform Temporal API where available.

concernImplementations.observability: A global ErrorHandler reporting to the platform's telemetry sink, plus an HTTP interceptor that attaches and propagates the correlation id the backend expects.
concernImplementations.health-and-readiness: Not applicable to a browser bundle. The build must emit a version stamp the running app exposes, so a support report identifies the exact deployed build.
concernImplementations.configuration: A typed config object provided through an InjectionToken and populated at bootstrap. Never import environment.ts deep inside a component.
concernImplementations.secrets-management: There are no secrets in a browser bundle. Anything requiring a secret goes through a backend endpoint; treat every value shipped to the client as public.
concernImplementations.authn-authz: Functional guards on lazy routes with canMatch so the chunk is never fetched when unauthorised, plus an interceptor attaching the token. The client-side check is a UX affordance — the server enforces.
concernImplementations.input-validation: Typed reactive forms with validators; mirror the server's rules but never rely on the client's copy.
concernImplementations.error-contract: Parse the backend ProblemDetails shape into a typed error and render field-level messages from it rather than a generic toast.
concernImplementations.resilience: An interceptor applying timeout and retry with backoff to idempotent GETs only.
concernImplementations.data-migrations: Not applicable. Persisted client state in localStorage or IndexedDB needs a version key and a migration path, or a stale shape breaks the app after a deploy.
concernImplementations.testing: Vitest or Jest for units with the Angular testing harness; Playwright for end-to-end. Test signal state through the component's public surface rather than reading internals.
concernImplementations.supply-chain: Committed package-lock.json, npm audit or an equivalent in CI, and a build-time bundle-size budget in angular.json.
concernImplementations.ci-gate: ng build --configuration production, ng test, ng lint, tsc --noEmit under strict, and the bundle budget — all required for merge.
concernImplementations.api-contract: Client types generated from the backend's OpenAPI document, never hand-written and never allowed to drift.
concernImplementations.rollback: Immutable, content-hashed asset filenames so a rollback does not serve a stale index.html against new chunks.

testing.unit: Vitest or Jest with the Angular testing harness
testing.integration: Component tests with a mocked HTTP layer

runtime.cadence: Roughly one major a year with frequent minors.

architecture.default: App Router with React Server Components by default. Client components only where interactivity actually requires them, marked at the leaf rather than the top of the tree.
architecture.why: Server components keep data fetching and secrets on the server and ship no JavaScript for the non-interactive majority of a page. Marking 'use client' at the top of a route pulls the entire subtree into the client bundle, which silently discards the benefit — hence the leaf rule.
architecture.escalateTo: Move to a separate backend service when the API is consumed by something other than this web app, or when its scaling profile diverges from page rendering.

concernImplementations.observability: OpenTelemetry through the instrumentation.ts hook, with structured server-side logging and a correlation id propagated into downstream calls.
concernImplementations.health-and-readiness: A route handler returning liveness, and a readiness handler that checks the database and any dependency the app cannot serve without.
concernImplementations.configuration: Environment variables parsed and validated with a schema at module load, so a missing variable fails the build rather than the request. Only NEXT_PUBLIC_ values reach the client.
concernImplementations.secrets-management: Server-only modules marked with the server-only package; secrets injected by the platform. Never a NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix on a secret.
concernImplementations.authn-authz: Checked in middleware for coarse routing and re-verified in every server action — a server action is a public HTTP endpoint regardless of which component calls it.
concernImplementations.input-validation: A schema validator such as Zod at the top of every server action and route handler, before any other work.
concernImplementations.error-contract: error.tsx and not-found.tsx boundaries per route segment; a typed JSON error shape from route handlers, never a raw exception.
concernImplementations.resilience: AbortSignal.timeout on every outbound fetch, with retry limited to idempotent requests.
concernImplementations.data-migrations: Owned by the ORM (Prisma or Drizzle), committed, applied by a deploy step rather than at request time.
concernImplementations.testing: Vitest for units, Playwright for end-to-end including server-action paths.
concernImplementations.supply-chain: Committed lockfile, dependency scanning in CI, and a bundle-size check on the client payload.
concernImplementations.ci-gate: next build, tsc --noEmit, eslint, tests, and a dependency scan — all required for merge.
concernImplementations.api-contract: Route handlers documented via a generated OpenAPI document when consumed externally; server actions typed end to end and not treated as a public contract.
concernImplementations.rollback: Immutable deployments with instant revert; expand-then-contract on schema so the previous build still runs.

architecture.default: Vite build, feature-folder structure, a server-state library for anything fetched, and local state kept local. Routing with a type-safe router.
architecture.why: The distinction that matters is server state versus client state: they have different lifecycles, and the standard failure is putting fetched data in a global client store, which then needs manual cache invalidation nobody maintains. Feature folders keep a change's blast radius visible in the tree.
architecture.escalateTo: Move to a meta-framework when SEO, first-paint latency, or server-side data access starts driving the design. Retrofitting SSR onto a mature SPA is substantially harder than starting there.

runtime.name: Node.js

architecture.escalateTo: Split a service out when it needs independent scaling and owns its own data. A shared database between two services is a distributed monolith with extra latency.

runtime.name: Terraform or OpenTofu
runtime.cadence: Frequent minors. Note the licence change that produced OpenTofu — confirm which of the two this project actually uses before quoting a version.

architecture.default: Composable modules with a thin root per environment, remote state with locking, and versions pinned for both the CLI and every provider.
architecture.why: Unpinned providers mean the plan you reviewed and the plan that applies can differ, which defeats the purpose of reviewing a plan at all. State without locking allows two concurrent applies to corrupt it, and that failure is discovered by finding resources nobody can account for.
architecture.escalateTo: Split state when a single apply grows slow enough that people start avoiding it, or when blast radius needs to be bounded by environment or domain.

runtime.name: Kubernetes
runtime.cadence: Three releases a year; roughly a one-year support window per minor, so this rots quickly.

architecture.default: Kustomize bases with per-environment overlays, or a Helm chart with per-environment values. Every workload declares resource requests and limits, probes, and a non-root security context.
architecture.why: A workload without resource requests is unschedulable in any predictable way and will be the first thing evicted under pressure. Overlays keep the environment difference visible as a small diff instead of three near-identical copies that drift apart.
architecture.escalateTo: Adopt a GitOps controller when manual kubectl application becomes the audit gap — at that point the cluster's actual state is no longer derivable from the repository.

modernCapabilities.insteadOf: The removed PodSecurityPolicy

concernImplementations.configuration: ConfigMaps mounted or projected as environment variables; the checksum annotated on the pod template so a config change triggers a rollout.
concernImplementations.secrets-management: An external secrets operator or sealed secrets; never a plaintext Secret in git.
concernImplementations.authn-authz: Least-privilege RBAC per service account, and a default-deny NetworkPolicy per namespace.
concernImplementations.input-validation: Admission policy — a validating admission policy or an OPA/Kyverno rule enforcing the required fields.
concernImplementations.error-contract: Not applicable at the manifest layer.
concernImplementations.resilience: Multiple replicas, a PodDisruptionBudget, topology spread, and correctly configured probes.
concernImplementations.data-migrations: A Job or an init container gated so it runs once per release, never on every pod start.
concernImplementations.testing: kubeconform for schema validation, a policy scan, and helm template or kustomize build diffed in CI.
concernImplementations.supply-chain: Image digests pinned, images signed and verified at admission, and an SBOM per image.
concernImplementations.ci-gate: Render, kubeconform, a policy scan such as Kyverno or Checkov, and a diff posted for review before apply.
concernImplementations.api-contract: Not applicable at the manifest layer.
concernImplementations.rollback: kubectl rollout undo verified in a non-production environment, plus a documented data-repair path for anything the rolled-back version wrote.

baselines.notes: stack-mappings.json already lists kubectl delete, kubectl apply -f and helm uninstall as forbiddenCommands enforced by the destructive gate. This baseline does not relax that.

baselines.name: Unknown / generic

architecture.default: None. Nothing was detected, so there is no baseline to apply. Read the repository, report what you actually find, and ask before asserting any architecture.
architecture.why: A guessed baseline in an unrecognised stack is worse than no baseline, because it is indistinguishable from a recorded decision once it is written down. Golden rule G6 applies directly: an honest 'not found' outranks a plausible guess.
architecture.escalateTo: Once the stack is identified, add it to config/stack-mappings.json and give it a baseline entry here in the same change.

concernImplementations.observability: The stack-independent concerns above still apply. Name how this project satisfies each one, or record it as an open gap.
concernImplementations.health-and-readiness: Ask. Do not assume a mechanism exists.
concernImplementations.secrets-management: Ask — and scan for committed credentials regardless of stack.

baselines.notes: This entry exists so that 'unknown' resolves to an explicit instruction to stop and ask, rather than falling through to whichever baseline happens to be first in the array.
